the plan and README note 13c document this as an intentional scope decision, not a defect. === END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS === === FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro === - TASK_GAP Requirement: The linked issue (#5618) states "Apply the same fail-closed target-branch and identity checks before supplying merged PR state to label reconciliation and wave status." The implementation gates five paths (reconcile loop, validation-dispatch wave gate, stall-recovery tag, backward-scan promotion, validation fix-up backfill). The consensus TASK_GAP entry notes that `reconcile_managed_issue_labels` (at `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4221-4295`) does not strip the `ai:merged` label when the reconcile loop rejects a merged PR through the target-branch gate — the Python helper at L4247 only adds `ai:merged` when `pr_merged=true`, and when `pr_merged` is falsy it does not remove an existing `ai:merged`. The labels JSON that feeds `check-wave-status` at L19993-19996 retains the old label, so an issue whose `ai:merged` was applied by a previous (vulnerable) poll cycle while this PR was not yet deployed could still appear merged in wave status on the first cycle after deployment. The PR correctly prevents all NEW wrong applications; this is a deployment-time consideration rather than an ongoing code defect, and a one-time cleanup of pre-existing wrongly-labelled wave children (if any exist) before this merges into consumers would close the window. Expected change site: `reconcile_managed_issue_labels` in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (Python heredoc at ~L4247–4263) — the `elif` branch could additionally strip `ai:merged` when `pr_merged` is falsy and a label-contract phase group member is the forced terminal label. Evidence of absence: At L4257–4263 the code only adds `ai:merged` when `pr_merged` is true; when `pr_merged` is false and `issue_state=open`, neither `ai:merged` nor `ai:closed` is added or removed. An existing `ai:merged` that was applied by a vulnerable cycle survives unchanged. severity=high | confidence=[4] === END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro === === FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash === - TASK_GAP Requirement: The PR description records completion PR #5885 as merged on 2026-10-01. GitHub repository slugs are case-insensitive, so case discrepancies could result in unexpected rejection. Suggested minimal fix: Normalize repository names to lowercase before comparison. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1 === END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash === === FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 === - File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh Line or code reference: 19978-19993 (current-wave reconcile loop); scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:4256-4263 (reconcile_managed_issue_labels); scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:2293-2305 (check-wave-status) Problem: The new target-branch gate (line 19978-19982) only prevents the *next* poll from adopting a wrong-base merge. It never removes `ai:merged` already applied by the previous vulnerable path, and it never downgrades an already-stored `status: "merged"` in the state file. After this PR ships, an issue that was incorrectly tagged `ai:merged` by a wrong-base `Fixes #` PR before the fix is still tagged, and `check-wave-status` will keep returning `merged`: - `reconcile_managed_issue_labels` (orchestrate_lib.py:4256-4263) only forces `ai:closed` when `pr_merged=False` AND `issue_state="closed"` AND no `ai:merged`/`ai:closed` is already present. With `issue_state="open"`, an existing `ai:merged` is never removed, even when the only linked PR was just rejected as `non_target_base`. - `check-wave-status` (orchestrate_lib.py:2293-2305) has the rule "stored terminal state never regresses" (line 2294) and returns "merged" from the `ai:merged` label (line 2303-2304) ahead of every other signal. Why it fails at runtime: A wave child whose earlier `ai:merged` came from a wrong-base `Fixes #` PR keeps that label forever. `check-wave-status` returns "merged" (source `label_ai_merged` or `stored_terminal`), `PR_MERGED` is reset to `false`, but the label/state is not, so `WAVE_COMPLETE=true` and the wave advances with the child's work never done. This is the exact exploit the PR claims to fix, just for issues already poisoned before rollout. severity=critical | confidence=[5] - File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh Line or code reference: 19564-19572 (backward-scan promotion); compare to 19573-19582 (the still-promoting branch) Problem: The backward-scan branch has the same cleanup gap. The new code adds the `if [ -n "${_pw_pr_target_reject}" ]` branch that only *logs* `[backward-scan] # ai:ready-to-merge; linked PR #

is merged but rejected=...` and *continues*. It never removes an `ai:merged` label that the vulnerable code may have written on a prior poll, never reverts a stored `status: "merged"` in the state file for the prior wave, and never resets the label/issue-state for downstream `close_merged_issues_sweep`. A prior-wave child that was promoted to `ai:merged` by the old logic keeps the label, and a future `close_merged_issues_sweep` run will close the child thinking it is done. Why it fails at runtime: The fix prevents new promotions but does not heal already-promoted issues. The PR is a security fix and the project must converge to a state where no wave child carries `ai:merged` from a non-target-base merge; today the fix only stops the bleed, it does not drain it. severity=critical | confidence=[5] - File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh Line or code reference: 16344-16379 (standalone stall recovery) and 17390-17533 (managed stall recovery) Problem: When `_reconcile_merged_pr_issue` returns 1 with `_rmpi_stall_action="run"`, the new code increments the stall budget via `STALL_RECOVERY_SHOULD_INCREMENT="true"` in the managed path (line 17422) and via the standalone path's `phase_attempts` block (line 16367-16373). But it does not address the case where the issue *was* previously tagged `ai:merged` by the vulnerable code (e.g. before this PR shipped, or in the prior AI-merge-resolve round that already tagged). The rejection path leaves the prior `ai:merged` label in place; `check-wave-status` still returns "merged" for that issue; the wave advances; the counted "attempt" cannot prevent it. Why it fails at runtime: The attempt-counting change is meant to keep the recovery ladder moving per AD-8/Q7:A, but the underlying wave-status signal still reads "merged" from the label, so the issue can advance while the stall recovery keeps spinning. severity=high | confidence=[4] - TASK_GAP Requirement: The PR description's "Gate evidence" table claims "Validation:
